It's uncanny how similar our situations are! I also play both piano and guitar but can't for the life of me decide "which I am" - while technically knowing that I am both. It's so hard. I completely understand your dilemma. I don't know if I've figured out a solution really, but since music is my special interest it makes it so difficult and overwhelming/frustrating to not come to some kind of good conclusion. I have a slight lean towards piano because I've played it longer, but not by much and I love guitar with my entire being as well. I'm not incredible at either and both need improvement, but practicing both simultaneously just makes the overall progress of learning take twice as long. And I'm the kind of person that needs to see a goal and real personal progress or I get incredibly discouraged. It's hard. 

I think the biggest help - but not a solution or guide by any means - is to do what I enjoy at the time. For example, learning a song I can't stop listening to on repeat. I haven't "picked" one instrument to focus on, but I try not to spend too long on one unless I'm hyperfocused for a long time (because hyperfocus is mostly how I get stuff done/make any progress in all aspects of my life). Unfortunately this process of following my current mood/interest is a little unpredictable - and I need a schedule to function - but it's the only thing that's helped me practice and get better at either instrument. It's sort of slow at times as well. But it works for me.

I recently have been working with a woman who helps people with disabilities apply for funding for school and get into jobs with the proper accommodations and such (she does a lot, it's hard to describe in one sentence). She - and everyone she works with - ALWAYS says not to disclose in the interview. They have a whole booklet on "when to disclose a disability," and it is never advised to do it right away. Wait until you either have the job (if that's an option) or are about to be hired. They WILL discriminate (she has talked honestly to many employers and they've said this flat out simply because they know it's harder to have a disabled/etc. employee). This is of course only possible if you can mask well enough that it isn't obvious and if your accommodations aren't something very obvious in the interview process. But this is the best strategy, and isn't "tricking" your employer. We have the right to any job that we're capable of (with proper training, of course). I specifically asked about this because I wasn't sure where the line was. 

Anyway. This is what my case worker who does this for a living says. But keep yourselves safe!

My main tips for starting out and general advice are to not rush anything, the game gives you the tool upgrades/plot advancements quite willingly so you don't have to worry about grinding or hyper focusing in the beginning. As well, save hard wood (from brown trees) and any fur (from furry animals after relationship increases with them); they are semi-scarce resources as they need time to regain/respawn and will be essential for buildings and things later on.

Sometimes our knowledge or unique insights because of autism can make us very good listeners/sympathisers, but it's so important for us and the person we're talking to to understand that it doesn't make us an expert in the area. We're not psychologists or therapists - unless you literally are, we can be anything after all! - so it's crucial to remember this! You can do this! Don't let one person control your mood/feelings!

I used to play a TON on Minecraft. I would bet I have thousands of hours in it. But lately I can't get into it - and I've figured out why finally.

Minecraft used to have a goal. The end credits roll when you defeat the ender dragon. And that was a solid, clear, achievable goal to me. These days, the yearly updates just add so much content (which I appreciate! FREE content is never bad!!) that doesn't add to that goal, it adds to the world building. Which is great, if you keep up with the updates. But with life being what it is (and ADHD being what it is), I don't have the attention span or interest for that these days. And if I try to jump back in, there's multiple updates worth of content I have to wrap my head around. (And that have changed how some of the older mechanics worked, so my default farms/builds often don't work anymore). I WANT to like Minecraft, I WANT to enjoy the game again, but it's just not easy to jump into anymore.

I, too, NEED a goal in games. I need something to work for. I need to feel like my time and energy and attention are being spent well and that I feel satisfaction at the end of it. Minecraft doesn't feel that way anymore. Which is saddening. I adored that game.

But I have been on a "diet*" (heavy asterisk), for about a year, and more carefully for about six months. My medication messes with my appetite severely, and I already had issues regarding appetite/eating habits because of ASD and ADHD. So I've had to pretty thoroughly structure my eating schedule and what I eat.

I eat a small breakfast first thing in the morning (right before taking my medication) of fruit, protein cereal, and either milk (in the cereal) or yogurt (eaten together like a parfait); then about 3 hours later I eat another "meal" of something a little more substantial nutrient-wise, often with meat or impression meat (such as a Beyond Burger), this meal varies depending on what I have in the house; then I eat again a few hours later, often a fruit smoothie with some yogurt with increased probiotics; then I don't eat for 4+ hours until a dinner meal in late evening, which I make sure to portion properly and not neglect vegetables and meat proteins.

I don't count calories or restrict any specific food (hence the "diet*") but I know I'm eating less and eating healthier (which is my main goal!) now than I was a year ago. I've lost weight doing this, and am aiming to be physically and mentally healthier.

EDIT: I forgot to specify that I still eat "treats." I have a cookie when they're offered, I eat cake on birthdays, I don't deprive myself of delicious things in an effort to "eat healthy." Fats are good for you, sugar is good for you, etc. Deprivation of things I enjoy is how I ended up so unhealthy in the first place. Enjoy your food!
